text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Coalition partners disagree on a proposed draft law on raising the compulsory education to eight years from five years.
- Turkey's state sugar company raises retail sugar prices by an average 35 percent.
MILLIYET
- The government is preparing a change in legislation regarding incentives for foreing capital, and foreign investments worth $500 million will begin in western Turkey.
- The government will prepare a economic stability package.
HURRIYET
- The last member of Tansu Ciller's "A team" of the True Path Party leaves the party.
- Foreign Minister Ismail Cem briefs the press on new targets for Turkey's foreign policy.
YENI YUZYIL
- The military is seeking ways to interrogate former deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller and interior minister Meral Aksener without lifting their parliamentary immunities.
RADIKAL
- The first crisis in the government. Finance Minister Zekeriya Temizel and state minister in charge of economy, Gunes Taner, disagree over authority to raise value added tax rates.
CUMHURIYET
- A total of 26,000 people have been killed since an emergency rule was imposed in southeast Turkey 10 years ago to quell a rebel Kurdish violence.
DUNYA
- Cotton producers protest to planned cotton purchase prices to be announced by buying cooperatives.
ZAMAN
- The Turkish Airlines handles an average 10,000 calls a day for flight bookings during busy summer months.
($1 = 154,350 Turkish lira)
